items.title: 13.10.1 Reaction with cold aqueous sodium hydroxide

source_refs.note: Topic 13.10.1 with the Keep in Mind box, printed page 300.

blocks.text: Chlorine disproportionates with cold aqueous sodium hydroxide, forming sodium chloride and sodium chlorate(I), NaClO (formerly called sodium hypochlorite): Cl2(g) + 2NaOH(aq) gives NaCl(aq) + NaClO(aq) + H2O(l). The oxidation states of chlorine are 0 in Cl2, -1 in NaCl and +1 in NaClO: chlorine is oxidised from 0 to +1 in NaClO and reduced from 0 to -1 in NaCl (the print writes 'to 1'), the simultaneous oxidation and reduction that makes this a disproportionation.

blocks.prompt: Show that the reaction of Cl2 with cold aqueous KOH is a disproportionation (Quick Check 13.5b).
blocks.explanation: Cl2 + 2KOH gives KCl + KClO + H2O. Chlorine starts at 0; in KCl it is -1 (gained an electron, reduced) and in KClO it is +1 (lost an electron, oxidised). The same element is both oxidised and reduced in one reaction, so it disproportionates.

items: Cold NaOH: Cl2 + 2NaOH gives NaCl + NaClO + H2O; Cl 0 to -1 (reduced) and 0 to +1 (oxidised); NaClO = sodium chlorate(I) (hypochlorite).
